tutorial: No FreeCAD wiki tutorial covers ScanRuler's Reverse engineer (Stefan Hermann's / CNC Kitchen's feature engine, ported onto Part / OCCT). The model rebuilds the simplest tutorial-style part — a block with a bored hole and rounded upright edges, as PartDesign's Basic_Part_Design_Tutorial.md builds one with Pad, Pocket and Fillet — through the feature list, so every volume has a worked-out answer; then a second body, a clearance, an imported STEP gauge block and a revolved ring.

expected.ids: In a fresh document the features get ids 1 to 11 in the order added (a refused call uses none): Base sketch 1, Block 2, Hole sketch 3, Bore 4, Round 5, Peg sketch 6, Peg 7, Seat dowel 8, gauge 9, Ring sketch 10, Ring 11.
expected.where: The argument shapes, ids, refusals and parameter answers were run in plain Python on the add-on's stand-in kernel on this pass; the volumes are worked out by hand. No geometry ran: the kernel is FreeCAD's Part.

placeholders.<UPRIGHT_EDGES>: a list of four whole numbers: the index of each edge in the reverse_body_describe { body: 'Block' } answer just before whose kind is 'line', length 20 and mid [0 or 40, 0 or 30, 10] (the block's corners; NOT the bore's seam, whose mid is at y 15)
placeholders.<MOVED_PEG>: the id of the 1000 mm³ body in the answer of the moveBody call (7 if a move keeps the body's id, 8 if the move makes it its own)

conventions.session: A fresh document: the ids above depend on it. Run the chunks in order.
conventions.health: Every changing reverse_ call carries health; it is red when a feature failed (the add-on's own reading, new on this pass). Expected green throughout.
